claim_summary: At each fixed sample size \(n\ge2\), the high-bandwidth limit \(a^3R_{n,a}\) exists almost surely with tail \(\mathbb P(Z_n>z)\sim(n-1)/(nz)\), whereas \(a^3\mathbb E R_{n,a}\sim2(n-1)\log(a)/n\).
integrity: The statistic and its fixed-bandwidth large-n null theory are credited to their original sources. Verification includes independent finite numerical checks; the analytic proof, not numerical testing, supports the infinite claims. No authorship or external certification is asserted.
limitations: Fixed n and maximum-likelihood-fitted Rayleigh scale only; not a joint n,a limit, alternative-estimator theorem, test-power result or claim of independent validation. Literature priority may require broader independent review.
title: A logarithmic high-bandwidth mean anomaly for the scale-fitted Rayleigh Stein test
